whereby the Ld. Trial Court discharged respondent no.3/G.B. Chadha under Section 498A/406/34 IPC.
Respondent no.2/Vivek Chadha and respondent no.4/Suman Chadha were also discharged under Section 406/34 IPC.
It was also held that charge only under Section 498A/34 IPC was made out against respondent no. 2 and 2.
Necessary facts for deciding the instant revision are that revisionist got married with to respondent no. 2 on 28.04.2017.
Respondent no.3 and 4 are her father-in-law and mother-in-law respectively.

6. In Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander and Another, (2012) 9 SCC 460, Hon'ble Apex Court also held that the object of section 397 CrPC is to set right a patent defect or an error of jurisdiction or law.

The revisional jurisdiction of the higher court is very limited one and where the Court is dealing with the question as to whether the charge has been framed properly and in accordance with law in a given case, it may be reluctant to interfere in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction.

In Dilipsinh (supra), it was held that at the stage of consideration of charge/discharge the court must proceed on an SUBHASH assumption that the material which has been brought on record KUMAR MISHRA by the prosecution is true and evaluate said material in order to KUMAR MISHRA determine whether the facts emerging from the material taken on its face value, disclose the existence of the ingredients necessary of the offence alleged.

Perusal of the complaint of the revisionist shows that no specific allegation has been levelled against respondent no3/G.B. Chadha.
It is nowhere mentioned that he had committed any physical or mental cruelty against the revisionist.
It is also nowhere mentioned that the clothes, jewelry or any other articles of the revisionist were entrusted to him.
Therefore, Ld. Trial court rightly discharged him from the case.

9. In the complaint, it is again nowhere mentioned that the clothes, jewelry or any other articles of the revisionist were entrusted to respondent no. 2 and 4 i.e. to Vivek Chadha and Sonam Luthra Vs.
Vivek Chadha Page no.7 of 9 Suman Chadha respectively.
Therefore, Ld. Trial court rightly discharged them also under Section 406 IPC.

10. Facts of Maya (supra) are not applicable to this case because in the said case, appellant had stated that on the first night of marriage itself, she had entrusted the custody of all her jewelry to the respondent for safe keeping and the same was misappropriated by respondents to discharge their financial liabilities.

However, in the instant case there is no allegation of entrustment of jewelry and clothes by the revisionist to the respondents and there is also no allegation of the misappropriation of the said articles by the respondents.

11. However, in the complaint, it is mentioned that the SUBHASH respondent no.4/Suman Chadha used to taunt the revisionist for KUMAR MISHRA not getting enough dowry from her parents and used to demean by SUBHASH her and her family.

It is also mentioned in the complaint that when the servant had gone to his native place, revisionist was made to do household works by respondents no. 2 and 4 beyond her physical capacity and she was allowed to attend her official work only after finishing the household works.

It is also alleged in the complaint that when she complained about the same to the respondent no. 2, he mocked her saying that his mother/respondent no. 4 had been doing the household works for so many years.

It is also alleged that when the parents of the Sonam Luthra Vs. Vivek Chadha Page no.8 of 9 revisionist came to her matrimonial home, revisionist was scolded because her parents had come there without advance intimation.

It is further alleged in the complaint that while going to dinner in the car, respondent no. 2 stopped the car in between and swtiched off the AC after closing the windows and doors, which made the revisionist claustrophobic and suffocating.

12. Therefore, there is prima facie material on record to frame charge against respondent no. 2 and 4 for the offence punishable under Section 498A/34 IPC.
13.
Having discussed as above, this court finds that the impugned order is correct and does not suffer from any illegality or impropriety and therefore, needs no interference.
Accordingly the impugned order is upheld and the revision stands dismissed.
